driver.description: The active cause of some happening within the system.

terms.control_point: Contact between a subject and object whereby power or influence can be exerted.
terms.conduit: A path along which actors are expected to move.
terms.amplifier: A combination of factors or process that increases the magnitude of an effect.
terms.repeller: An object that pushes other objects away from itself.
terms.enabler: A contributory cause; can encourage change.
terms.dampener: A combination of factors or process that reduces the magnitude of an effect.
terms.cycle: A repeating process or iterative effort towards a goal.
terms.genator: The original impetus or trigger of a sequence of events.
terms.cascade: A sequence of knock-on effects; a chain reaction.
terms.inflection: A turning point or critical juncture.
terms.equifinality: Multiple activities lead to the same outcome.

signal.description: Communication that can potentially trigger some action.

terms.framing: Interpretive paradigm which makes the system understandable.
terms.monitor: Active scanning of a process or domain to compare with an expected state.
terms.indicator: Indirect or partial signal of status; a symptom of a deeper cause.
terms.feed_back: Information about the outputs of an action are routed back as inputs.
terms.status_display: Regularly updated information about a particular object.
terms.alert: A warning signal intended to mobilize a response.

state.description: A condition of a system or objects within it.

terms.stock: A discrete collection of consumable or expendable resources for future use.
terms.standard: A set of items made more or less uniform; conformity to criteria.
terms.redundancy: Multiple stockpiles or parallel sub-systems that act as a back-up.
terms.fault_recovery: Correction or compensation that minimize impact of faults.
terms.tipping_point: The threshold beyond which rapid, large-scale change happens.
terms.criticality: The threshold beyond which a dynamic becomes self-sustaining.
terms.load: A stock of items being moved under containment conditions.
terms.mutation: A reconfiguration of an object caused by an error or exogenous factor.
terms.transition: Changing from one state to another.
terms.accumulation: The build-up of items or experiences over time.
terms.capacity: The finite ability to handle a particular quantity of activity.
terms.reset: Returning to original conditions or earlier state.
terms.replication: When an object is copied, reproduced, or divided.
terms.assembly: Building blocks with which system structures are formed.
terms.separation: The division of a part into two or more parts.
terms.maintenance: The restoration of operations after a malfunction.

boundary.description: Separates different parts of a system.

terms.gate: A controlled opening in a barrier.
terms.buffer: A boundary or zone that diminishes, delays, or otherwise alters a driver.
terms.reactive_boundary: A boundary that responds to forces and acts as an actant.
terms.permissions: The control of activity within a bounded area.
terms.container: A boundary that groups and isolates objects.
terms.semi_permiable: A barrier that blocks some objects while allowing others.
terms.divider: A boundary that keeps two or more distinct objects apart.
terms.protector: A barrier preventing damage by blocking unwanted forces.
terms.edge: Outer boundary that defines the scope of domain or system.

relation.description: The dynamic between two or more objects in a system.

terms.group: An affiliated collective of actors that share patterns of behavior.
terms.rank: The hierarchical status bestowed on an object or actor.
terms.differentiation: A contrast between other items or actors in a system.
terms.mediation: The mitigation or reconciliation of conflict between parties.
terms.aggregate: A group of objects or actors of the same type.
terms.coupling: The tightness or looseness of ties between parts of a system.
terms.network: An arrangement of interconnected parts that interact directly.
terms.cluster: Elements defined as a group by virtue of proximity.

domain.description: The context in which the system (or parts thereof) exists.

terms.reference_points: Features in the context that can act as orienting devices.
terms.resources: The availability and access to the factor inputs needed.
terms.levels_of_scale: System attributes at different orders of analysis.
